name: Bean and Nothingness
meta: RBOR Games · C++ / SDL / OpenGL · shipped Dec 2021
body: A tile-based logic-puzzle game. As co-lead programmer I built the replay / undo / state-saving system, a GUI level editor shipped publicly via Steam Workshop, and a custom sound mixer, and contributed across the core game loop and entity logic. name: CoNDOR Rating & Matchmaking
meta: Open source · Python / C++ / MySQL / PuLP · multiple seasons through 2022
body: A Bayesian rating and matchmaking system for a multi-league competitive season, rebuilt and refined over several seasons. I wrote a custom paired-comparison model — Gaussian priors plus binomial match evidence, fit by MAP estimation with hand-derived gradients and a hand-written optimizer — chose its prior variance by maximizing likelihood on held-out matches from an earlier season, and — judging normal tails too thin for real performance — gave it a heavier-tailed link function whose tail weight is fit to past results. Series forecasts account for correlated rating uncertainty, which meant patching a C++ Bayesian Elo engine to expose its covariance matrix. Weekly pairings are solved as an integer program that maximizes the entropy of the predicted result, so every match is as informative as possible.

name: Necrobot
meta: Open source · Async Python / MySQL / Google Sheets · 2015–present
body: Two production Discord bots — race management and full league-season administration for Crypt of the NecroDancer — built from one layered codebase of roughly 150 modules across 16 packages with a documented, acyclic dependency order. Async Python over MySQL, with an internal command framework, a table-mapped object layer, Google Sheets integration for standings, timezone-aware scheduling, and TrueSkill-based ratings. In continuous community use for over a decade.
